fields.description: The message sender field is made up of the sender EORI and branch. The Branch ID/Sub Office is a 10-digit number and is a required field for S&S GB messages. The Branch ID is a number that the trader adds and is not something HMRC provides. An EORI is made up of a country code, to show where the organisation or individual is registered, and a unique code or number. For UK businesses the number is made up as follows (with a few minor exceptions): VAT registered businesses: GB + VRN (VAT registration number) + 000 Non-VAT registered businesses: GB + unique number issued by HMRC The IE315 requires the MesSenMES3 field to be populated with an EORI/Branch ID combination similar to this: GB000000000012/0000000010

The message recipient field is optional and is made up of the recipient EORI and branch. The branch is a 10 digit number. An EORI is made up of a country code, to show where the organisation or individual is registered, and a unique code or number. For UK businesses the number is made up as follows (with a few minor exceptions): VAT registered businesses: GB + VRN (VAT registration number) + 000 Non-VAT registered businesses: GB + unique number issued by HMRC
This is for the date of preparation submitted by the trader system in DDMMYY format.
This is for the time of preparation submitted by the trader system in GMT in HHMM format.
This is an alphabetic field which contains the priority of the ENS declaration.

This is generated by the declarant system and is used for message tracking. The message ID is included in the message response and is a unique reference for the message. The message ID is restricted to a maximum of 14 characters.
This field will contain the CD (Common Domain) and number. It will be CC315A or CC313A.
This field is required for response and rejection messages. It does not apply for one-way messages.

The Local Reference Number (LRN) should be a reference generated by the declarant. It will be used by HMG to identify the specific entry summary declaration if there are any queries around the submitted declaration before it has been accepted and a movement reference number (MRN) issued. Therefore it must be unique per declarant submitting the declaration (‘Person Lodging’). It is validated using the ‘Person Lodging’ EORI for declarations which have been submitted. Note: Where an amendment is made, the MRN from the original declaration should be used.
This section contains the Movement Reference Number. Field mandatory for Amendments only.

Enter the appropriate mode of transport code corresponding to the active means of transport in which the goods are expected to enter the customs territory of the Community. See Mode of Transport . For all accompanied movements via the Channel Tunnel the appropriate mode of transport code is 3 (Road). Where air cargo is transported on modes of transport other than air, the other mode of transport shall be declared. However, IATA number must be completed in the Conveyance Reference Number field and Airway bill number must be provided in Transport Document Number .

fields.fieldName: Identity of Means of Transport Crossing Border
fields.description: This field, where appropriate, contains the identity of the means of transport or, if containerised, the equipment identification number. For maritime, the IMO ship identification number to be included. For rail, the wagon number to be included. Not to be used for air - the IATA flight number should be included in the data field Conveyance Reference Number . For accompanied roll-on roll-off, the Vehicle Registration Number to be included. Road (Channel Tunnel), the Vehicle Registration Number to be included. For unaccompanied roll-on roll-off, the IMO ship identification number to be included.

Total number of items declared in the Entry Summary Declaration. If present, it must equal the total number of goods items provided and must not have leading zeros.

Enter figures of the total number of packages for goods declared within declaration. This must be the total number of packages as per the ‘Kind of Packages’ declared. In the case of bulk items, this is the number of ‘containers’, ‘wagons’, or ‘hulls’ that the goods are stored in. This is an optional field. If present: this number must equal the sum of all ‘Number of packages’ +‘Number of pieces’ provided at goods item level + 1 for any declared as bulk this number must not have leading zeros

Note: The Specific Circumstance Indicator field has the following rules: value ‘E’ (AEO) can be used only if the ‘Person Lodging’ the Summary Declaration and all ‘Consignees’ declared in it have a valid AEO certificate of type ‘AEOF’ or ‘AEOS’ if the submission is an amendment submitted by a Representative, then the Representative is also required to have a valid AEO certificate of type ‘AEOF’ or ‘AEOS’ declarant EORI must be GB and will always be provided. The UCN/UCR must be provided by Fast Parcel Operators and Express Operators, to enable the identification of the consignment. If further reference numbers are available to support identification of the declaration for commercial purposes, use this field. Commercial Reference Number needs to follow the WCO (World Customs Organization) recommended format: year (2 digits), EORI, another commercial ref (for example Invoice number or waybill number) this is issued by industry in order to identify specific goods (a particular consignment) within a load of multiple consignments, and can be used by Border Force for identification of consignments Note: this is not a required field but if entered the user will not need to provide transport document numbers.

This field should be provided for all modes except accompanied RoRo, unaccompanied RoRo, and road movements. You should provide information to identify the journey of the means of transport for example, voyage, flight or trip number, if applicable. For Sea and Maritime (‘Transport mode at border’ = ‘1’), where the conveyance reference number is used, and the first four digits consist of ‘XFER’ in uppercase, then it must be followed by the lorry registration plate number, without any separator between ‘XFER’ and the lorry plate. Otherwise ‘XFER’ cannot be used in the first four digits of the conveyance reference number. For Air (‘Transport mode at border’ = ‘4’), the IATA number should be included. The format is alphanumeric 8, and must contain the carrier code (AN3), the flight number (N4) and an optional suffix (a1) without any separator between the two or three elements. For Rail, the train number is to be provided.

Place of Loading is used for the identification of the seaport, airport, freight terminal, rail station or other place at which the goods are loaded onto the means of transport being used for their carriage, including the country where it is located. This must be provided at either header or item level. If provided at header level, it cannot be provided at item level. If provided at item level, it must be provided for every item. For unaccompanied goods the place of loading will be the port of departure. The first 2 digits of the place of loading shall be the Country Code from the code list, detailing the country where the goods were loaded onto the means of transport. See Country Code . This should be followed by the name of seaport, airport, freight terminal, rail station or other place at which goods are loaded onto the active means of transport that will cross the border. Format validation is limited to alphanumeric 35. For Accompanied RoRo and Road (Channel Tunnel) goods the place of loading is the Freight Terminal, Warehouse or Other place of loading onto the trailer/container which will be the active means of transport that will cross the border. In these circumstances you should provide the first 2 digits of the Country Code from the code list, followed by the name of the warehouse or other place and then the post code. Format validation is limited to alphanumeric 35.

Place of unloading is used for the identification of the seaport, airport, freight terminal, rail station or other place at which the goods are unloaded. This must be provided at either header or item level. If provided at header level, it cannot be provided at item level. If provided at item level, it must be provided for every item. For unaccompanied goods the place of unloading will be the port of arrival. The first 2 digits of the place of unloading shall be the Country Code from the code list, detailing the country where the goods will be unloaded from the means of transport. See Country Code . This must then be followed by the name of the seaport, airport, freight terminal, rail station or other place at which goods are unloaded from the active means of transport used for their carriage to be presented to customs. Format validation is limited to alphanumeric 35. For Accompanied RoRo and Road (Channel Tunnel) goods the place of unloading is the Freight Terminal, Warehouse or Other place of unloading off the trailer/container which was the active means of transport at the border. In these circumstances you should provide the first 2 digits of the Country Code from the Code list, followed by the name of the warehouse or other place and then the post code. Format validation is limited to alphanumeric 35.

Date at which the respective entry summary declarations were issued and when appropriate, signed or otherwise authenticated. Date and time of declaration submitted Must be provided by trader system This must be Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) The timestamp in this format: YYYYMMDDHHMM (for example: 202102090749)

fields.fieldName: Declaration Date and Time of Amendment
fields.description: This is for the date and time of the declaration amendment submitted by the trader system and must be GMT (Greenwich Mean Time). The timestamp in this format: YYYYMMDDHHMM (for example: 202102090749)

The true consignor address must be provided and in the following format: Name/ Company, Building Number, Street, Town, Region, Postcode, Country. If the consignor EORI or Trader Identification Number (TIN) is held, this should also be provided. If a GB EORI is provided, the name and address fields are not required and must not be supplied.

The number of the item in relation to the total number of items contained in the declaration.

This is a plain language description precise enough for customs to be able to identify the goods without reference to other documents/materials. General terms such as ‘consolidated’, ‘general cargo’, ‘parts’ or ‘miscellaneous’ should not be provided. Providing an inaccurate or general description of the goods may lead to unnecessary delays, such as physical examinations of goods to ascertain their real nature. For examples of terms that should be included, refer to Acceptable Goods Descriptions . The tariff chapter heading should not be used as a substitute for a plain language goods description.

fields.description: You should include the weight (mass) of goods including packaging, but excluding the carrier’s equipment. This should be entered in kilograms, up to 3 decimal places where necessary. This data should be provided at item level as well as header level.

Transport charges method of payment code - this information is only to be provided where available The following codes can be used: A - Payment in cash B - Payment by credit card C - Payment by cheque D -Other (e.g. direct debit to cash account) H - Electronic credit transfer Y - Account holder with carrier Z - Not pre-paid

This section is for container Information

This field must be provided when containers or trailers are being moved. If a container is being moved on a trailer then the container number should be entered into this field in preference to the registered trailer number. The unique Container or trailer number (letters or numbers) which identifies the container/trailer is to be entered. However, where multiple consignments are carried in a single container provision of Marks and Numbers will assist identification of the relevant cargo and minimise delays. In particular this must be provided for Maritime Containers, Road (Channel Tunnel), Accompanied RoRo, and Unaccompanied RoRo. The Trailer number provided should be the trailer number registered with the respective national authority in the country of registration. (Refer to Trailer Registration Tab for details of your respective national registration schemes.

Specify the appropriate package type from the list of available codes found in Kinds of Package .

You should include the number of individual items packaged in such a way that they cannot be divided without first undoing the packing; or number of pieces if unpackaged. This information does not need to be provided where goods are in bulk. Where more than 1 of the same type of bulk is included in a movement, this should be included in this field.
You should include the number of individual ‘pieces’ if unpackaged. If ‘type of package’ indicates bulk, number of pieces is not required This field must not contain leading zeros

This field must be provided for all packaged goods. You should provide a free form description of the marks and numbers on transport units or packages for all packaged goods, including any information and descriptions that will enable the easy identification of individual packages. If the goods are ‘loose’ within a transport container (ie a vehicle or bulk grain in a sea container), then this field need not be completed and the container number must be provided in the ‘Container Number’ field.

Note: As this information is only collected at header level it is important that all consignments included in the declaration have followed the same routing. The country routing list should include the countries of departure and destination.

The First Entry Customs Office Reference. See Location codes for ports of entry in Great Britain . Codes are structured as follows: the first 2 characters (a2) serve to identify the country by means of the country code the next 6 characters (an..6) stand for the office concerned in that country Codes will be set up for the identification of all potential customs offices of first entry.

fields.fieldName: Expected Date and Time of Arrival
fields.description: The time must be GMT. Scheduled date and time of arrival of means of transport at: (air) first airport (Road) ‘Channel Tunnel’ arrival at the Eurotunnel terminal in Coquelles, France sea, unaccompanied RoRo, and accompanied RoRo) arrival at first port (rail) arrival at Dollands Moor freight yard The scheduled date and time of arrival is a static reference point. It should be the same on all entry summary declarations submitted for consignments on that vessel, aircraft, train, or vehicle regardless of whether they are submitted by the carrier or by representatives on their behalf. Representatives should, therefore, obtain this information from the carrier .

This section relates to the entry carrier, which is the party that transports the goods at entry into the customs territory. This must be completed if the carrier is different from the person lodging the entry summary declaration. The person lodging the declaration must ensure they have the carrier’s ‘knowledge and consent’ to submit the entry summary declaration on their behalf. The carrier’s EORI/TIN must be provided. If a GB EORI is provided, then the name and address are not required. If a non-GB EORI/TIN is provided, then the carrier’s details must also be provided in the following format: Name/Company, Building Number, Street, Town, Region, Postcode, Country.
